correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the nonempty power-semigroup product, characterized idempotents as exactly rectangles, and recovered every support fiber through the intrinsic square map. Strict monotonicity in support dimension is proved by a proper graph injection. Every cardinality-preserving pair of projection permutations and every fiber bijection yields a homomorphism, and all automorphisms are exhausted. The semidirect splitting uses fixed canonical fiber labels, and the factorial order follows from orbit sizes. Verified boundary dimensions and checked all 2880 constructed automorphisms of \(P^*(B_{2,2})\) for all products. General results rely on proof, not finite checks.

value.rationale: The nonempty-set power construction is a basic functor on semigroups and singleton preservation is a named contemporary rigidity problem. This theorem gives a natural complete classification for every finite rectangular band, a sharp two-sided versus one-sided boundary for singleton preservation, and an exact huge factorial automorphism-group census. It exposes non-induced automorphisms in a family not covered by the inverse-semigroup rigidity theorem and structurally explains them via support-fiber symmetries; this is not just an isolated small computation. Historical priority remains qualified.
